hypotheses: nu > 0 (arbitrary positive viscosity)
entries.conclusion: There exist f in C^inf_c(R^3 x (0,inf); R^3), a compact K subset R^3, and smooth (u,p) on R^3 x [0,1) solving d_t u + (u.grad)u - nu Lap u + grad p = f, div u = 0, u(.,0) = 0, with supp u(.,t) U supp p(.,t) subset K for all 0<=t<1, sup_{0<=t<1} ||u(t)||_{L^2} < inf, and limsup_{t->1} ||u(t)||_{L^inf} = inf. Consequently no smooth (u,P) on R^3 x [0,inf) with the same force and datum has uniformly bounded kinetic energy.
constants: nu > 0 (universally quantified; obtained from nu = 1 by the rescaling (10.22))
cites: proved in Section 10.4 from Proposition 10.1, Lemma 10.3, Lemma 10.4, Lemma 10.5 and Theorem 3.1(iv)
entries.role: The main theorem: Fefferman alternative (C), with the exhibition clauses (compact support of u and p, bounded energy, limsup blowup) stated alongside the non-existence clause. Section 2 has no numbered statements.

hypotheses: viscosity nu = 1 (the local construction)
the similarity coordinates (3.2): tau = q(1-eta^2), z = q^D eta, X = r^2/(2q), with A = 1/2 + h, D = 1/2 - h
entries.conclusion: There are constants 0 < h < 1/100, q_* > 0, 0 < X_a < X_ext < inf and smooth fields on Omega_* = {tau > 0, q < q_*} with: (i) u = curl A + B e_theta with A, B e_theta smooth in Cartesian coordinates at the axis, exactly divergence-free; (ii) every Cartesian space-time derivative of A, B e_theta, p uniformly bounded on compact spatial sets with c <= q <= c' < q_*, up to the one-sided boundary tau = 0, with compatible limits; (iii) flatness |d_x^alpha d_t^b R(u,p)| <= C_{alpha,b,N,X_1} q^N on 0 <= X <= X_1 as q -> 0 (3.4), and for X >= X_ext the residual is identically zero with A = 0, B = K(r,tau) = r^{-1-2h} H_ext(tau/r^2), p = -int_r^inf K^2/rho drho (3.5), K solving the radial swirl heat equation -d_tau K = d_rr K + r^-1 d_r K - r^-2 K; (iv) for some X_in in (0, X_a) and e_0 > 0, u_theta(sqrt(2 X_in tau), 0, 0, 1 - tau) = tau^-A (e_0 + O(tau^2h)) as tau -> 0 (3.6).
constants: H_ext smooth on [0,inf) with bounded derivatives
cites: proved from Theorem 4.6, Proposition 5.5, Proposition 9.9 per Section 3.4 and Section 9.5
entries.role: The local theorem: the whole of Sections 4-9 exist to prove it. Its four clauses are exactly what Section 10 consumes -- (i) for the potential cutoff, (ii) for the cutoff-transition limits, (iii) flatness for the force extension, (iv) for the blowup path.

hypotheses: a leading field (velocity and pressure) given in cylindrical coordinates for t < 1; or a scalar auxiliary profile in (X, eta)
entries.conclusion: 'Regular at the axis' means: the velocity and pressure extend smoothly across r = 0 in Cartesian coordinates for t < 1; for a scalar profile, a smooth extension in (X, eta) to X = 0.
cites: Section 3.1 (E/sqrt(2X), U, V_0/X smooth at X = 0)
used by Theorem 4.6(i), Proposition B.2, Proposition 10.1
entries.role: Fixes what axis regularity means for the whole construction; every 'smooth at the axis' clause later refers here.

hypotheses: alpha >= 0, beta > 0 two parameters in a chain of constant choices
entries.conclusion: alpha << beta means alpha/beta is required sufficiently small, the allowed size depending on all data already fixed; in a chain of constants, choices proceed from right to left; small reciprocals specify large parameters; for expressions depending on profile variables the smallness is uniform on the stated domain.
cites: used throughout Sections 6-9 for the order of parameter choices (h, N, k, epsilon, S_*, ...)
entries.role: The order-of-choices convention. It is what makes 'sufficiently small' claims in Sections 6-9 well-defined, and a mis-ordering here would be a circularity in the constants.

hypotheses: f a smooth profile of (X, eta); b real; the similarity relations (4.1): tau = q(1-eta^2), z = q^D eta, X = s/q, s = r^2/2, d = 1-eta^2, L = 1-2h eta^2, 0 < h < 1/2
entries.conclusion: d_t(q^b f) = q^{b-1} T_b f and d_z(q^b f) = q^{b-D} Z_b f, where T_b f = L^{-1}(-b f + D eta f_eta + D_X f) and Z_b f = L^{-1}(2 b eta f + d f_eta - 2 eta D_X f), D_X = X d_X (4.2).
cites: chain rule from q_t = -L^-1, eta_t = D eta/(qL), X_t = X/(qL), q_z = 2 eta q^{1-D}/L, eta_z = d/(q^D L), X_z = -2 eta X/(q^D L)
entries.role: The conversion of physical t and z derivatives into similarity-variable operators; every residual computation in Sections 4-5 runs through it. Also fixes that q is uniquely determined for tau > 0 with |eta| < 1.

hypotheses: profiles E, U, Pi satisfying the incompressibility and radial-balance identities (4.7), with phi, U, Pi smooth at the axis and phi > 0
Q_s, N_s the solutions of (4.9) extending smoothly to X = 0 (i.e. C_Q = C_N = 0 in (4.10))
the leading tangential residuals R^(0)_theta, R^(0)_z of (4.12), which retain radial viscosity and drop axial viscosity
entries.conclusion: R^(0)_theta and R^(0)_z are minus the cylindrical divergences (d_r + 2/r) and (d_r + 1/r) of the physical stress q^{-A-1/2} T_0, with T_0 = F(p_s - s), p_s = (X Q_s/L, X N_s/(L E)), s = (a, -b_s), a = 2 - 2l, b_s = 2 D_X U/E (4.11). The equations for vanishing leading residual stress are -2 L X phi_XX + 2 phi_X = S_q phi and -2L(X U_XX + U_X) = S_n (4.13).
entries.role: THE STRESS IDENTITY: it converts the leading residual into the divergence of a two-component annular stress, which is the object the pulses (Proposition 7.5) must realize. Section 3.2's stress representation is this proposition.

hypotheses: Q_s, N_s the solutions of (4.9) with C_Q = C_N = 0
the five cumulative integrals M, I, J, S, C_p of (4.15)
entries.conclusion: Q_s = -W + [(1-h) I - D eta I_eta - d J_eta + 2(h-D) eta J]/(X H) and N_s = -W U + [D(M - eta M_eta) + 4 h eta S - d S_eta]/X + 4 A eta Pi - d Pi_eta (4.16).
constants: W = 1 - 2 D eta A_X(U) - d d_eta A_X(U)
cites: integration by parts on d_X(XW) and on Pi_X = E^2/(2X)
entries.role: Expresses the integrated inviscid residuals through the five cumulative integrals, which is what makes 'match five integrals at a join' sufficient (Lemma 4.4).

hypotheses: two profile pairs (U_i, E_i), i = 1,2, smooth on (0,inf) x [-1,1] with E_i > 0, whose five integrals (4.15) are smooth including one-sided eta-derivatives
one common smooth axis pressure Pi_ax(eta) with Pi_i = Pi_ax + C_{p,i}
(i): (U_1,E_1) = (U_2,E_2) for X >= X_h and Delta m(X_h, eta) = 0
(ii): a rectangle R = [X_0, X_1] x [-1,1], k >= 0, e_min > 0 with E_i >= e_min on R
entries.conclusion: (i) m_1 = m_2 and Pi_i, V_{0,i}, Q_{s,i}, N_{s,i}, p_{s,i}, a_i, b_{s,i}, T_{0,i} agree for all X >= X_h. (ii) ||Delta(Q_s, N_s, p_s)||_k <= C_k(||Delta(U,E)||_{k+1} + ||Delta m||_{k+1}) (4.17), with C_k depending only on k, h, X_0, X_1, e_min, the C^{k+1} norm of Pi_ax and a common bound for (U_i, E_i, m_i) in C^{k+1}; NO radial derivative of a difference occurs.
constants: the norm ||f||_j = max over eta-derivative orders <= j of sup over R
cites: used by Proposition C.2 (radial modulation) and in Steps 1-3 of the proof of Theorem 4.6
entries.role: THE JOINING LEMMA. (i) is the exact identity that lets an inner profile be glued to a prescribed outer one by matching five numbers per eta; (ii) is the estimate that lets the shear be changed violently (N log X modulation) while p_s moves only O(1/N). Both are load-bearing for Theorem 4.6.

hypotheses: a > 0, b_s real, p_s = (p_{s,1}, p_{s,2}) in R^2; t_s, v_s, P_c, J_c defined by (4.20)
first assertion: v_s > 2
second assertion: a compact K subset {a > 0} in (a, b_s, w) with a - b_s w > 0 and 2 b_s w + b_s^2/a + (a-2) w^2 < 2 on K
entries.conclusion: If v_s > 2, the admissible stress cone condition ((4.21) with v_s > 2) is equivalent to P_c > v_s and (v_s - 2) J_c^2 < 2 (P_c - v_s)^2 (4.22). For every such K there is P_K > 0 such that every p_{s,1} >= P_K with p_{s,2} = w p_{s,1} satisfies the relaxed cone condition (4.21), and the admissible one if also v_s > 2.
cites: used by Proposition A.4 (outer construction) and Lemma 4.11 (loop shear)
entries.role: Makes the cone condition a pair of inequalities in profile variables and gives the sufficient large-p_{s,1} criterion the outer construction uses. The cone is what Proposition 7.5 needs to find two wave families with positive weights.

hypotheses: none beyond the framework of (4.1)-(4.11): it is an existence theorem for the profiles
entries.conclusion: There exist fixed h in (0,1/100), lambda > 0, C > 1, 0 < X_a < X_b and profiles E, U, Pi on X >= 0, |eta| <= 1 such that: (i) F = phi/C, U, Pi, V_0/X are smooth on [0,R] x [-1,1] for every R, phi > 0, E > 0 for X > 0, analytic in eta on [0, X_an], Pi normalized to vanish at infinity (4.25); (ii) the radial balance Pi_X = E^2/(2X) and the residual identities of Proposition 4.2 hold exactly, T_0 = 0 for X <= X_a and X >= X_b and nonzero in between, (4.13) holds on [0, X_a]; (iii) F, a, v_s - 2 have positive lower bounds on the closed annulus and the unit direction n = T_0/|T_0| extends smoothly to it with the margin (4.26) for a fixed kappa in (0,2), n(X_a) parallel to (a, -b_s), n(X_b) = (1,0), b_s(X_b) = 0; (iv) a flat radial-edge weight zeta with |T_0| >= c zeta and |d^alpha T_0| <= C_alpha zeta delta^{-m_alpha} (4.27); (v) the four moment identities M(inf) = J(inf) = S(inf) = 0 and int (H - H_pow) dX = 0 (4.28), and for X >= X_b the exact heat exterior U = V_0 = 0, E = c_inf X^{-A} H(2d/X) with H(Z) = Gamma(1+h)^{-1} int_0^inf e^{-v} v^h (1+Zv)^{-h} dv (4.29); (vi) two reserved intervals I_pos, I_mean in (X_a, X_v) on which U = 0 and E = c_patch (1+eta^2)^{-1} X^{-1/2-lambda} (4.30).
cites: Propositions A.4, A.7, A.10, B.2, B.3, B.5, B.8, C.2, C.3 and Lemmas A.5, A.6, A.8, B.7, C.1 through those
entries.role: THE LEADING PROFILE THEOREM. The whole of Appendices A, B, C exist to prove it. Everything downstream -- Section 5's corrections (needs (i),(ii),(vi)), Proposition 7.5 (needs (iii)), the wave supports (need (iv)), Lemma A.8/heat exterior (needs (v)) -- consumes one of its six clauses.

hypotheses: alpha_1,...,alpha_m distinct reals; beta_1,...,beta_m nonnegative nonzero smooth functions with ordered disjoint compact supports in (0,inf)

second part: B(eta) a smooth invertible matrix on [-1,1], Q_eta a smooth bilinear map, d smooth, integer k >= 0, with 8 nu_j^2 q_j ||d||_{C^j} <= 1 for j = 0, k, where nu_j is the C^j norm of multiplication by B^{-1} and q_j the bilinear norm of Q
entries.conclusion: B_ij = int_0^inf x^{alpha_i} beta_j(x) dx is invertible, with bounded inverse and parameter derivatives over a smooth compact family. The equation B(eta) c + Q_eta(c,c) = d(eta) has a smooth solution, unique in ||c||_{C^0} <= 2 nu_0 ||d||_{C^0}, with ||c||_{C^k} <= 2 nu_k ||d||_{C^k}; when Q = 0 it is c = B^{-1} d with no smallness.
constants: nu_j, q_j, the radii r_j = 2 nu_j ||d||_{C^j}
cites: Rolle's theorem / generalized Vandermonde sign argument
used in Step 3 of Theorem 4.6, Proposition B.8, Proposition C.2, Lemma 5.2, Lemma 8.7
entries.role: The finite-dimensional moment solve. Every 'restore the five integrals with bumps' step in the paper is an instance of it. Its invertibility rests on distinct exponents, which is why lambda > 0 matters.

hypotheses: parameters chosen in the order M_d, then P_*, then lambda, then h, with T_d = e^{M_d} + 10, P_* > e^{T_d}, 0 < h < min{1/100, lambda, e^{-T_d}}
entries.conclusion: There are smooth outer profiles (U_o, E_o) on (0,inf) x [-1,1], E_o > 0, such that with x = X/X_R, f = (1+eta^2)^{-1}: (i) U_o = 4 eta and E_o = P_* f x^{1/10} for 0 < x <= 1, and the pressure datum Pi_0(eta) = -int_0^inf E_o^2/(2X) dX (4.31) is independent of X_R, analytic and even, with Pi_0 <= -(5/2) P_*^2 f^2 and eta Pi_0' > 0; (ii) four ordered disjoint intervals I_j = X_R(alpha_j, beta_j) with X_R < X_good < inf I_1, sup I_4 < X_v < X_tail < X_b = e^3 X_tail, on which U_o = 0 and E_o = c_patch f X^{-1/2-lambda} on I_1, I_3, I_4; U_o = M_o = J_o = 0 for X >= X_v; M_o(inf) = J_o(inf) = S_o(inf) = 0 and int (H_o - H_pow) dX = 0; (iii) the relaxed cone holds on [e^{-5} X_R, e^{1/2} X_tail] and the admissible cone on [X_good, e^{1/2} X_tail], with positive gap minima that may depend on X_R; for X >= X_b, U_o = V_{0,o} = 0 and E_o = c_inf X^{-A} H(2d/X), whose physical swirl solves the radial swirl heat equation with K_r < 0.
entries.role: THE OUTER (EXTERIOR) PROFILE: fixes the axis pressure datum Pi_0, the exact heat exterior, the four moment identities at infinity, and reserves the intervals corrections will use. It is what the inner solution must join onto.

hypotheses: the family of Lemma 4.8 for every X_R >= R_*
a leading field regular at the axis, agreeing with that family for X >= X_tail, satisfying the four moment identities (4.28) as functions of eta, and having the canonical pressure (4.25)
entries.conclusion: Its physical stress T = q^{-A-1/2} T_0 satisfies T_theta(r) = r^{-2} int_r^inf r'^2 R^(0)_theta dr' and T_z(r) = r^{-1} int_r^inf r' R^(0)_z dr', so T_0 = 0 for X >= X_b. On e^{1/2} X_tail <= X < X_b the admissible cone holds with b_s = 0, 2 + h < a <= 2 + 2h, T_theta > 0 and 2 - (a-2)(T_z/T_theta)^2 >= kappa_o > 0. Near X_b, with y_b = log(X_b/X): T_{0,theta} = e^{-4/y_b^2} y_b^{-3} b_theta and T_{0,z} = e^{-4/y_b^2} y_b^3 b_z with inf b_theta > 0 (4.32). Uniform in eta; constants may depend on X_R but not on q.
constants: the outer-collar factorization functions b_theta, b_z of (4.32)
entries.role: Turns the moment identities at infinity into the vanishing of the stress OUTSIDE the annulus (integration from infinity instead of from the axis), and gives the outer edge factorization Theorem 4.6(iv) needs.

hypotheses: the outer-profile data of Lemma 4.8 and a prescribed finite collection of eta-derivative orders
axis parameters j_0, delta_*, sigma_*, Lambda, transition length T_sh, amplitude threshold C_0 chosen; any C >= C_0; then X_a = 4/Lambda, X_R = 110 (C P_*)^{10}, X_h = X_R e^{-5}
after C: an activation width t_1, a shear factor kappa_0, and the remaining transition widths
entries.conclusion: There are profiles E = sqrt(2X) phi/C, U, Pi = Pi_0 + C_p on [0, X_h] x [-1,1] with: (i) phi > 0 and phi, U, Pi, V_0/X smooth including X = 0, analytic in eta on [0, X_an] for some X_an in (X_a, X_h), solving (4.13) on [0, X_a] with T_0 = 0 there; (ii) a > 0, P_c > 2, v_s < U(P_c,J_c) on (X_a, X_h], v_s > 2 on the first collar (X_a, X_an], a(X_a) > 0 and v_s(X_a) > 2 + c_ex, with the inner-collar factorization T_0 = e^{-t_1^2/y_a^2} g_a(y_a) B_a(y_a, eta) (4.33), B_a(0,eta) = F(X_a,eta) s(X_a,eta) != 0, and derivative bounds |d^alpha T_0| <= C_alpha e^{-t_1^2/y_a^2} y_a^{-N_alpha}; (iii) near X_h the fields equal U_0 = 4 eta, E_0 = P_* f x^{1/10} and the five integrals m(X_h, eta) = m_0(X_h, eta) of that reference pair (4.34), with the same axis pressure Pi_0. X_R may exceed any further lower bound without altering Lambda, T_sh.
constants: the tolerance eps_m and width omega_fin
entries.role: THE INNER (AXIS) PROFILE: the stress-free analytic core solving (4.13) on [0, X_a], continued outward and moment-matched to the reference pair at X_h. Together with Lemma 4.8 it supplies the two pieces Theorem 4.6's proof joins.

hypotheses: I = [X_-, X_+] compactly inside (0,inf); a, b_s, p_s smooth on I x [-1,1] with a > 0; t_s, v_s, P_c, J_c by (4.20)
P_c > 2 and v_s < U(P_c, J_c) throughout the rectangle (the relaxed cone); v_s > 2 in neighbourhoods of both radial endpoints
entries.conclusion: There is a smooth period-one family (a_L, -b_L)(X, eta, phi), phi in R/Z, with int_0^1 (a_L, -b_L) dphi = (a, -b_s), such that every loop shear satisfies the admissible cone with p_s held fixed: Psi_i(a_L, b_L, p_s) >= mu_L > 0 for i = 1..4 (4.36); near both radial endpoints the loop is independent of phi and equals (a, -b_s).
constants: the map Psi(a,b,p) = (a, v-2, c-v, 2(c-v)^2 - (v-2) j^2) of (4.35)
entries.role: Where only the RELAXED cone holds (the joining interval), replaces the shear by a periodic loop of the same mean every value of which is ADMISSIBLE. Step 2 of Theorem 4.6 then realizes this loop at a large frequency N log X.

hard_pages.why: The parameter chain on p.40 -- 0 < C^-1 << T_sh^-1 << Lambda^-1 << sigma_* << delta_* << j_0 << eps_m << h << lambda << P_*^-1 << M_d^-1 << 1, then omega_fin << t_1 << kappa_0 << C^-1, then N -- is twelve nested 'sufficiently small' choices whose ORDER is the whole content (Definition 3.3), and it is stated in one line with no table of which lemma consumes which. Reconstructing which constraint comes from Lemma 4.8, which from Proposition 4.10, which from the moment solve (Lemma 4.7's 8 nu^2 q ||d|| <= 1) and which from the Lipschitz margin (4.41) took three passes. Also: Step 2's shear modulation E_N = E_0 exp(A(X,eta,N log X)/N) changes a, b_s by O(1) while changing U, E by O(1/N) -- the reason Lemma 4.4(ii) is stated WITHOUT radial derivatives of differences -- and that dependency is only visible once you see (4.39)-(4.40) together.

Two long statements whose proofs are one-paragraph pointers into Appendices A and B; every constant (M_d, T_d, P_*, X_R = 110 (C P_*)^10, X_h = X_R e^-5, X_i = 110, j_0 <= .05, the tolerance eps_m) is introduced here but justified only in the appendix, so on a first pass they read as arbitrary. The value X_R = 110(CP_*)^10 in particular is not motivated until (4.34)'s hat-normalization is understood.
